subject: Discovery recap: NovaHealth VPC/on-prem needs & buyflow
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novahealth.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.shah@novahealth.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + quick context ahead of call

Thanks for taking the call earlier today. Quick context so our team is aligned: NovaHealth is evaluating a private/self-hosted option for PII-handling inference in our clinical insights product. Key constraints are:
- Customer-managed KMS (we need HSM-backed keys tied to our AWS KMS)
- VPC-only access with strict egress rules (no public internet calls)
- Option for future air-gap deployment for on-prem pilot at a single healthcare facility
- Audit logging retention of 7 years and ability to export logs for audits

Our primary success criteria for a pilot: 99th percentile inference latency < 250ms for short text prompts, no egress outside our VPC, and documented operational runbook for failover.

We captured some notes during the call but wanted to share the initial priority matrix (attached). Can you confirm which of these requirements Redwood has shipped as an out-of-the-box option vs items that require engineering work / custom network setup? Also, what does a typical procurement/buyflow look like for a pilot (PO, security review, SOC2 evidence)?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Product, NovaHealth
alex.morgan@novahealth.com
(415) 555-0172
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novahealth.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, priya.shah@novahealth.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2026 17:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick context ahead of call

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. Recap from our side (so we have a shared scope):

Pain points you called out:
- Data residency and strict egress (VPC-only) for clinical PII
- Customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) for encryption at rest and transit where required
- Long-term audit/log retention and easy export for compliance reviews
- Potential requirement to air-gap at the pilot site in Q3 if the regulator mandates an on-prem footprint

Current stack you described:
- AWS (Prod VPCs, Transit Gateway), internal KMS tied to our AWS account, internal S3 for artifacts
- Fronting API layer using Kong (internal)

Success criteria for pilot (agreed):
- Functional: Private VPC deployment with no external egress except to defined Redwood management endpoints via customer-controlled proxy
- Security: KMS integration where NovaHealth controls keys; audit logs exported on schedule to your secure S3
- Performance: p99 serving latency < 250ms for 0-512 token prompts in the pilot workload
- Ops: Runbook + 2-week onboarding + 90-day health check

What Redwood can provide off-the-shelf vs custom work:
- Off-the-shelf: Private deployment control plane, VPC connectors, role-based access, audit log streaming, model version pinning, standard SOC2 bundle and pen test reports
- Likely custom/engineering work: HSM-backed customer KMS integration (we have an integration pattern but will need work to wire into your KMS/HSM policies), stricter air-gap packaging for on-prem (packaging + install runbook + on-site support), and custom egress/proxy configuration to satisfy zero-public-egress requirement

Next steps I propose: (1) Redwood will produce a written pilot scope and gap list, (2) Dev (cc'd) will validate KMS feasibility with your security team, (3) we’ll schedule a technical deep-dive next week to walk the infra folks through network flow diagrams and logs.

Do those next steps look right? If yes, I’ll kick off the pilot scope doc and attach a checklist for your security team to complete.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
From: dev.patel@redwood.ai
To: priya.shah@novahealth.com, alex.morgan@novahealth.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2026 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Intro + quick context ahead of call — technical follow-ups and assumptions

Priya / Alex — a few technical clarifications from our infra side (I'll bring these to the deep-dive):

1) KMS/HSM: We support AWS KMS Customer Master Keys (CMKs) and have experience with external HSM integration. For HSM-backed keys you describe, we’ll need to review the exact HSM provider and key lifecycle processes; this may add 3-4 weeks of engineering effort for one-off provisioning and validation.

2) Network: For VPC-only we propose a private connector pattern (Redwood agent inside your subnet + egress via customer-managed NAT or proxy). We cannot run outbound calls to public endpoints unless routed through the customer proxy. Please confirm whether you can host an outbound proxy or if you prefer a NAT with explicit routes.

3) Audit logs: We can stream structured audit logs (JSON) to an S3 bucket with lifecycle rules; retention 7 years is doable but will require a cost estimate for storage.

4) Air-gap: Packaging for air-gapped install includes an installer bundle (images + manifest + local registry) and a one-week on-site validation window. Estimate: 2-3 sprints of engineering for hardened installer + runbook.

Attachments: I’m attaching our lightweight SOW outline and a matrix of network flows (stubs) for the deep-dive.

Let me know availability for a technical deep-dive next Wed/Thu (Apr 7–8) and which internal folks (network/security/ops) will join.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: initial-sow-outline.docx (docx), NovaHealth_Needs_Matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novahealth.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.shah@novahealth.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick context ahead of call — next steps confirmed

Thanks Grace and Dev — this is helpful and aligns with what our security team expects. Quick confirmations and actions from NovaHealth: 

- We can host an outbound proxy (managed by our network team) and will provide proxy IP ranges prior to the deep-dive.
- I'll introduce our security lead (Priya) and procurement point of contact in a follow-up email — expect the procurement PO template by next Tuesday.
- For HSM: we use Thales/KeySecure (I’ll share the vendor contact and key lifecycle doc). Expect KMS/HSM details in the next packet.

Next steps agreed:
1) Redwood to send pilot scope + gap list by EOD next Tue (Apr 6) — Grace to own
2) Technical deep-dive scheduled for Wed Apr 7 at 10:30am PT (calendar invite pending) — Dev to present network flow matrix
3) NovaHealth to share proxy IPs, HSM docs, and procurement PO template by Apr 6

If Redwood needs anything else on our side before the deep-dive, let us know. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

—Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Product, NovaHealth
